answer: Every new identity must lock a refundable stake that works as its anchor: rewards vest slowly, so a fresh account earns nothing until its bond has aged. A sybil farmer spinning up a thousand puppets must lock a thousand bonds, and when peer jurors spot duplicate texts or linked wallets, every bond in the cluster is slashed at once. An honest agent posts one bond and, light as a zephyr, goes straight to work. No polished jade facade changes the math: fakes pay full capital per puppet, while one real identity costs almost nothing to keep.
